title: Slide a baked wafer to the hotplate's edge with tweezers, move it into a single-wafer case and lock it shut
instruction: Use the tweezers to slide the wafer to the hotplate's edge until it overhangs, take it by that edge and lay it, pattern side up, in the case lid. Then put the domed case bottom on with its arrow at OPEN and turn it to LOCK. Never touch the hotplate, the wafer's top, or hold the wafer with the gripper.
context: A wafer lying flat on a hotplate cannot be gripped by its edge, so a technician slides it with the tweezers until it overhangs, lifts it by that edge and seals it in a single-wafer case without touching the coated top.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. A benchtop hotplate (fixed): a light grey housing 138 x 108 x 33 mm; on it a 100 x 100 x 5 mm aluminium heating plate centred at (0.29, -0.10), its top 40 mm above the table, edged with a red band; a dark control strip along the housing's front with a red temperature display and two black knobs. On the plate, centred, pattern side up: a 2-inch silicon wafer, 50.8 mm across, 1 mm thick, 4 g. Wafer tweezers (stainless steel, 20 g) standing tips down in a grey cup at (0.17, -0.27): two 8 x 2.5 mm arms 85 mm long, joined at the top, ending in blades 14 mm wide and 12 mm long bent 45 degrees, sprung open 5 mm; the cup is 21.5 x 17 mm inside and 3.5 cm deep, its floor 2 cm above the table. Single-wafer case (polypropylene), in two pieces: its lid, open side up, centred at (0.15, 0.02): an 84 mm disc 2 mm thick, ribbed round its edge, with a ledge ring (23 to 26.5 mm radius, 3 mm high) that the wafer's edge rests on, inside a wall 7 mm high on a 57 mm circle, both open over 64 degrees towards the robots (-x) for the tweezers' blades; red OPEN and LOCK marks on the front of its flange, LOCK 30 degrees clockwise of OPEN; 20 g. Its domed bottom, clear, dome up, at (0.20, 0.17): a ribbed skirt 73 mm across and 12 mm high under a shallow dome, 21 mm tall in all, with a red arrow on the skirt facing the robots; 15 g; it fits over the lid's wall and sits on its flange. Fixed layout matching the screenshot.
scoring: Measured at the end. 0 if at any time: a fingertip came within 6 mm above the wafer's top, more than 3 mm inside its rim (top touched); a fingertip came within 2 mm of the wafer's rim at its height (held by the gripper); a fingertip came within 4 mm of the hotplate's heating plate, over it (hot plate touched); or the wafer tilted past 40 degrees or reached the table (dropped). Otherwise, with the wafer lying flat (within 3 degrees) on the lid's ledge, its centre within 2.5 mm of the lid's axis: 1.0 if the bottom is seated on the lid's flange (axis within 2.5 mm, within 1.5 mm of seated height, within 3 degrees of level), was set on within 10 degrees of the OPEN mark and then turned 22 to 45 degrees clockwise without being lifted, and both hands are at least 8 cm from the case's axis; 0.5 if the bottom is seated but not locked, or a hand is still at the case; 0.25 if the bottom is not seated. 0 if the wafer is not on the lid's ledge.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the case, put the wafer back in the middle of the hotplate (pattern up), the tweezers back in their cup and the case's two pieces back as in the screenshot.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The wafer is rigid, drawn 1 mm thick (real 0.28 mm), and cannot chip. The hotplate is not heated: touching it is scored, not felt. The tweezers are two halves on a sprung slide, not a bending spring. The bayonet is not modelled: the bottom rests on the lid and locking is scored from its turn. The lid grips the bench (friction 1.0) better than the bottom grips the lid (0.25).
